chunks: I said: A well from which pieces of skin come out in its water. He (peace be upon him) said: It is of no consequence. The salamander sometimes sheds its skin. And he said: It suffices you to draw out a bucket of water.

key_terms.الْوَزَغ: Salamander or gecko; its shed skin falling into water does not render it impure
key_terms.بِئْر: Well (water well used for drinking or ablution)
key_terms.دَلْو: Bucket or container used to draw water from a well; drawing one bucket is the prescribed remedy
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْء: Legal formula meaning 'it is of no consequence' — a standard ruling that something does not cause ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is a well with pieces of skin in its water ritually impure in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the ritual purity of a well from which pieces of skin emerge. The Imam rules that such a well is not ritually impure, explaining that the skin pieces likely come from the natural skin-shedding of a salamander (wazagh). He further prescribes that drawing out one bucket of water is sufficient purification before using the well. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that water remains pure unless clearly contaminated, and that a practical remedial action suffices to restore normal use.
